# Tasks Document

## Phase 1: Configuration and Data Models

- [ ] 1.1. Add schedule and cleanup data models to models.py
  - File: src/publisher/models.py
  - Add RecurringSlot dataclass with day_of_week, time, timezone fields
  - Add ScheduleEntry dataclass with product_id, scheduled_time, platforms, post_id, status, created_at, slot_index
  - Add ScheduleConfig dataclass with min_post_spacing_hours, prevent_duplicates, allow_past_schedules, max_posts_per_day, timezone
  - Add CleanupConfig dataclass with enabled, verify_before_delete, require_all_platforms, archive_before_delete, archive_dir, keep_published_days, preserve_metadata, preserve_logs
  - Purpose: Define type-safe data structures for schedule and cleanup features
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/models.py (existing PublishResult, PublishMetadata, PublisherConfig patterns)_
  - _Requirements: 2, 3, 5, 6_
  - _Prompt: Role: Python Developer specializing in data modeling and type safety | Task: Add RecurringSlot, ScheduleEntry, ScheduleConfig, and CleanupConfig dataclasses to src/publisher/models.py following requirements 2, 3, 5, and 6, using existing dataclass patterns from PublishResult and PublisherConfig | Restrictions: Follow existing naming conventions, use type hints (datetime, Path, etc.), add __post_init__ validation where needed, maintain immutability for frozen dataclasses | Success: All dataclasses compile without errors, validation works correctly, follows existing model patterns, provides to_dict() methods for JSON serialization_

- [ ] 1.2. Extend PublisherConfig with schedule and cleanup configurations
  - File: src/publisher/config.py
  - Add schedule_config: ScheduleConfig field to PublisherConfig
  - Add cleanup_config: CleanupConfig field to PublisherConfig
  - Update load_publisher_config() to parse recurring_schedule, schedule_validation, and cleanup sections from YAML
  - Purpose: Integrate schedule and cleanup configuration into three-tier config system
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/config.py (existing load_publisher_config patterns), src/publisher/models.py_
  - _Requirements: 2, 3, 5, 6_
  - _Prompt: Role: Backend Developer with expertise in configuration management and YAML parsing | Task: Extend PublisherConfig with schedule_config and cleanup_config fields and update load_publisher_config() to parse new YAML sections following requirements 2, 3, 5, and 6, using existing configuration loading patterns | Restrictions: Maintain three-tier precedence (CLI > ENV > YAML), use existing YAML parsing utilities, validate configuration on load, handle missing sections gracefully with defaults | Success: New config fields are properly loaded, defaults work correctly, configuration validates on load, three-tier precedence is maintained_

- [ ] 1.3. Add schedule and cleanup sections to publisher.yaml
  - File: config/publisher.yaml
  - Add recurring_schedule section with enabled, timezone, and slots array
  - Add schedule_validation section with min_post_spacing_hours, prevent_duplicates, allow_past_schedules, max_posts_per_day
  - Add cleanup section with all CleanupConfig fields
  - Set all features to disabled by default for backward compatibility
  - Purpose: Provide configuration template for schedule and cleanup features
  - _Leverage: config/publisher.yaml (existing structure)_
  - _Requirements: 2, 3, 5, 6_
  - _Prompt: Role: DevOps Engineer with expertise in YAML configuration and system defaults | Task: Add recurring_schedule, schedule_validation, and cleanup configuration sections to config/publisher.yaml following requirements 2, 3, 5, and 6, using existing YAML structure and commenting patterns | Restrictions: Set all features disabled by default, provide example slot configurations in comments, use consistent indentation and naming, include helpful comments for each field | Success: YAML is valid and parseable, example configurations are clear and helpful, defaults ensure backward compatibility, all fields are documented_

## Phase 2: ScheduleManager Implementation

- [ ] 2.1. Create ScheduleManager class skeleton
  - File: src/publisher/schedule.py
  - Create ScheduleManager class with __init__, schedule_path, config, entries attributes
  - Implement _load_schedule() and _save_schedule() for JSON persistence
  - Implement get_next_slot() to calculate next recurring slot occurrence
  - Purpose: Establish schedule management foundation with file I/O and slot calculation
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/tracking.py (load_tracking, save_tracking patterns), src/publisher/models.py (RecurringSlot, ScheduleEntry)_
  - _Requirements: 2, 4_
  - _Prompt: Role: Python Developer with expertise in file I/O and datetime manipulation | Task: Create ScheduleManager class skeleton with JSON persistence and recurring slot calculation following requirements 2 and 4, using tracking.py patterns for file operations and RecurringSlot model | Restrictions: Use atomic writes (temp file + rename) for schedule.json, handle missing files gracefully, use zoneinfo for timezone support, ensure get_next_slot() respects day-of-week and time correctly | Success: ScheduleManager loads and saves schedule.json correctly, get_next_slot() calculates next occurrence accurately with timezone support, file operations are atomic and safe_

- [ ] 2.2. Implement list_scheduled() method
  - File: src/publisher/schedule.py
  - Add list_scheduled() method with platform, status, date_from, date_to filters
  - Filter entries list based on provided parameters
  - Sort results by scheduled_time ascending
  - Purpose: Provide calendar view with flexible filtering
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/schedule.py (self.entries from task 2.1), src/publisher/models.py (ScheduleEntry)_
  - _Requirements: 1_
  - _Prompt: Role: Python Developer with expertise in list filtering and datetime comparisons | Task: Implement list_scheduled() method with filtering and sorting following requirement 1, operating on self.entries list loaded from schedule.json | Restrictions: Filter efficiently without loading external data, handle None filter values correctly, ensure timezone-aware datetime comparisons, return sorted list by scheduled_time | Success: Filtering works correctly for all parameter combinations, None values are handled properly, results are sorted chronologically, timezone comparisons work correctly_

- [ ] 2.3. Implement auto_schedule() method
  - File: src/publisher/schedule.py
  - Add auto_schedule() method accepting videos, platforms, start_slot, dry_run parameters
  - For each video: extract product_id, check if already published, find next available slot
  - Create ScheduleEntry and validate with ScheduleValidator (will be implemented in Phase 3)
  - Call publisher.publish() with scheduled_time for each entry
  - Track summary: scheduled, skipped, failed counts
  - Purpose: Batch assign videos to recurring slots with validation
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/schedule.py (get_next_slot() from task 2.1), src/publisher/tracking.py (is_already_published), src/publisher/models.py (ScheduleEntry, Platform)_
  - _Requirements: 2, 4_
  - _Prompt: Role: Python Developer with expertise in batch processing and async operations | Task: Implement auto_schedule() method following requirements 2 and 4, using get_next_slot() for slot calculation, is_already_published() for duplicate detection, and creating ScheduleEntry objects | Restrictions: Respect start_slot parameter, skip already published videos, handle validation failures gracefully, use dry_run to preview without publishing, ensure async publisher.publish() is awaited | Success: Videos are assigned to correct slots starting from start_slot, already published videos are skipped, dry_run mode works without side effects, summary counts are accurate_

- [ ] 2.4. Implement add_entry() method
  - File: src/publisher/schedule.py
  - Add add_entry() method accepting ScheduleEntry
  - Validate entry (will integrate with ScheduleValidator in Phase 3)
  - Append to self.entries list
  - Call _save_schedule() atomically
  - Purpose: Atomic write operation for adding schedule entries
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/schedule.py (_save_schedule() from task 2.1), src/publisher/models.py (ScheduleEntry)_
  - _Requirements: 2_
  - _Prompt: Role: Python Developer with expertise in atomic operations and data integrity | Task: Implement add_entry() method with atomic write operation following requirement 2, using _save_schedule() for persistence | Restrictions: Ensure atomic write (temp file + rename), validate entry before adding, maintain entries list integrity, handle write failures gracefully | Success: Entries are added atomically without data corruption, validation prevents invalid entries, write failures don't corrupt schedule.json_

## Phase 3: ScheduleValidator Implementation

- [ ] 3.1. Create ScheduleValidator class
  - File: src/publisher/schedule_validator.py
  - Create ScheduleValidator class with __init__, config, existing_entries attributes
  - Implement validate() method as main entry point returning tuple[bool, str]
  - Implement _is_duplicate() helper checking (product_id, platform, scheduled_time) uniqueness
  - Implement _check_spacing() helper enforcing min_post_spacing_hours on same platform
  - Implement _check_daily_limit() helper enforcing max_posts_per_day
  - Purpose: Enforce all schedule validation rules
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/models.py (ScheduleConfig, ScheduleEntry), datetime module for timezone-aware comparisons_
  - _Requirements: 3_
  - _Prompt: Role: Python Developer with expertise in validation logic and datetime operations | Task: Create ScheduleValidator class with comprehensive validation following requirement 3, implementing duplicate detection, spacing enforcement, and daily limit checks | Restrictions: Use timezone-aware datetime comparisons, validate scheduled_time.tzinfo is not None, check duplicates based on product_id+platform+time, enforce spacing only on same platform, calculate daily limit by date component | Success: All validation rules work correctly, error messages are descriptive with suggestions, timezone validation prevents naive datetimes, spacing and daily limits are enforced accurately_

- [ ] 3.2. Integrate ScheduleValidator into ScheduleManager
  - File: src/publisher/schedule.py
  - Update auto_schedule() to create ScheduleValidator and validate each entry before publish
  - Update add_entry() to validate before appending to entries
  - Handle validation failures with descriptive error logging
  - Purpose: Prevent invalid schedules from being created
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/schedule_validator.py (ScheduleValidator.validate()), src/publisher/schedule.py (auto_schedule and add_entry from tasks 2.3 and 2.4)_
  - _Requirements: 2, 3_
  - _Prompt: Role: Python Developer with expertise in error handling and integration | Task: Integrate ScheduleValidator into ScheduleManager's auto_schedule() and add_entry() methods following requirements 2 and 3, validating entries before persistence or publication | Restrictions: Create new ScheduleValidator instance with current entries, handle validation failures without raising exceptions in auto_schedule (track in failed count), raise ValidationError in add_entry for immediate failures | Success: Invalid entries are rejected with clear error messages, validation failures in auto_schedule are tracked and logged, add_entry rejects invalid entries with ValidationError_

## Phase 4: CleanupManager Implementation

- [ ] 4.1. Create CleanupManager class skeleton
  - File: src/publisher/cleanup.py
  - Create CleanupManager class with __init__, outputs_dir, config, publisher, audit_log_path attributes
  - Implement _log_cleanup() to append to cleanup_audit.json with product_id, platforms, post_urls, cleaned_at, disk_freed_bytes, archive_path
  - Implement _calculate_dir_size() to compute total size of product directory
  - Purpose: Establish cleanup foundation with audit logging
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/models.py (CleanupConfig), src/publisher/tracking.py (JSON file patterns), pathlib for directory operations_
  - _Requirements: 5, 6, 8_
  - _Prompt: Role: Python Developer with expertise in file operations and audit logging | Task: Create CleanupManager class skeleton with audit logging following requirements 5, 6, and 8, implementing _log_cleanup() for JSON append and _calculate_dir_size() for disk usage | Restrictions: Use atomic writes for audit log (temp file + rename), handle missing audit log file gracefully, calculate directory size recursively including subdirectories, log all required fields (product_id, platforms, urls, timestamp, size, archive path) | Success: CleanupManager initializes correctly, _log_cleanup() creates/appends to audit log atomically, _calculate_dir_size() accurately computes directory size including all files_

- [ ] 4.2. Implement verify_publication() method
  - File: src/publisher/cleanup.py
  - Add async verify_publication() method accepting product_id and platforms
  - Load publish_history.json to get post_ids for each platform
  - For each platform: call publisher.get_status(post_id) to check status
  - Return tuple[bool, dict[str, str]] indicating if ALL platforms published and status map
  - Purpose: API-verified multi-platform publication check
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/tracking.py (load_tracking, get_publish_record), src/publisher/late/client.py (LatePublisher.get_status()), src/publisher/models.py (CleanupConfig.require_all_platforms)_
  - _Requirements: 5, 8_
  - _Prompt: Role: Python Developer with expertise in async operations and API integration | Task: Implement async verify_publication() method following requirements 5 and 8, using tracking.py to get post_ids and publisher.get_status() for verification | Restrictions: Use asyncio.gather() for concurrent status checks, respect require_all_platforms config flag, handle API failures gracefully (treat as unpublished), check for status == "published", return False if any platform failed or not published | Success: Verification correctly checks all platforms via API, concurrent requests work efficiently, API failures don't cause crashes, require_all_platforms flag is respected_

- [ ] 4.3. Implement archive_directory() method
  - File: src/publisher/cleanup.py
  - Add archive_directory() method accepting product_dir path
  - Create archive_dir if it doesn't exist
  - Use shutil.make_archive() to create ZIP of product directory
  - Name archive: <product_id>_<timestamp>.zip
  - Return archive path
  - Purpose: Backup product directory before deletion
  - _Leverage: shutil.make_archive, pathlib for directory creation, datetime for timestamps_
  - _Requirements: 8_
  - _Prompt: Role: Python Developer with expertise in file archiving and compression | Task: Implement archive_directory() method following requirement 8, using shutil.make_archive() to create ZIP backups | Restrictions: Create archive_dir if missing with parents=True, use UTC timestamp in ISO format for archive name, handle archive creation failures with descriptive errors, ensure ZIP contains all files and subdirectories | Success: Archives are created successfully in archive_dir, ZIP contains all product files, archive naming is consistent and sortable, failures provide clear error messages_

- [ ] 4.4. Implement cleanup() method
  - File: src/publisher/cleanup.py
  - Add async cleanup() method accepting product_id, platforms, dry_run
  - Check config.enabled, return early if disabled
  - Call verify_publication() if config.verify_before_delete is True
  - Call archive_directory() if config.archive_before_delete is True
  - Remove product directory with shutil.rmtree()
  - Call _log_cleanup() with all details
  - Return dict with success, message, disk_freed
  - Purpose: Execute single product cleanup with safety checks
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/cleanup.py (verify_publication, archive_directory, _log_cleanup from tasks 4.2, 4.3, 4.1), shutil.rmtree, pathlib_
  - _Requirements: 5, 8_
  - _Prompt: Role: Python Developer with expertise in file operations and error handling | Task: Implement cleanup() method with comprehensive safety checks following requirements 5 and 8, integrating verify_publication, archive_directory, and _log_cleanup | Restrictions: Check config.enabled first, skip cleanup if verification fails, create archive before deletion if configured, use dry_run to preview without deletion, handle permission errors gracefully, calculate disk_freed before deletion | Success: Cleanup executes safely with all checks, dry_run mode works without side effects, verification prevents premature deletion, archiving works before deletion, disk_freed is accurate_

- [ ] 4.5. Implement cleanup_all() method
  - File: src/publisher/cleanup.py
  - Add async cleanup_all() method accepting platforms and dry_run
  - Scan outputs_dir for all product directories
  - For each product: check if published to all platforms via tracking.py
  - Call cleanup() for each published product
  - Track summary: cleaned, skipped, disk_freed counts
  - Purpose: Batch cleanup of all successfully published products
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/cleanup.py (cleanup() from task 4.4), src/publisher/tracking.py (is_already_published), pathlib for directory scanning_
  - _Requirements: 6_
  - _Prompt: Role: Python Developer with expertise in batch operations and directory traversal | Task: Implement cleanup_all() method for batch cleanup following requirement 6, scanning outputs_dir and calling cleanup() for each published product | Restrictions: Use pathlib.glob() to find product directories, check publication status via tracking.py for all platforms, skip products not published to all platforms (if require_all_platforms=true), respect keep_published_days age filter if configured, limit concurrent cleanup operations to 3 | Success: All published products are identified and cleaned, skip count includes unpublished products, summary counts are accurate, concurrent operations don't exceed limit_

## Phase 5: CLI Integration

- [ ] 5.1. Add calendar list command to CLI
  - File: src/publisher/late/cli.py
  - Add calendar subparser with list action
  - Add --platform, --status, --date-from, --date-to filter arguments
  - Implement cmd_calendar() handler function
  - Create ScheduleManager and call list_scheduled() with filters
  - Display results with formatted output (product_id, scheduled_time UTC + local, platforms, status)
  - Purpose: Provide calendar view command for scheduled posts
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/schedule.py (ScheduleManager.list_scheduled()), src/publisher/late/cli.py (existing command patterns like cmd_list_accounts)_
  - _Requirements: 1_
  - _Prompt: Role: CLI Developer with expertise in argparse and user interface design | Task: Add calendar list command to CLI following requirement 1, using existing command patterns from cli.py and ScheduleManager for data | Restrictions: Follow existing argparse structure, parse date strings to datetime objects, display both UTC and local timezone times, format output with logger.info(), add --debug flag support, handle empty results gracefully | Success: Command parses arguments correctly, filters work as expected, output is well-formatted with both UTC and local times, empty results show helpful message_

- [ ] 5.2. Add schedule auto command to CLI
  - File: src/publisher/late/cli.py
  - Add schedule subparser with auto action
  - Add --outputs-dir, --platform (append), --start-slot, --dry-run arguments
  - Implement cmd_schedule_auto() handler function
  - Scan outputs_dir for videos, filter unpublished
  - Create ScheduleManager and call auto_schedule()
  - Display summary with scheduled, skipped, failed counts
  - Purpose: Provide auto-scheduling command for batch video assignment
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/schedule.py (ScheduleManager.auto_schedule()), src/publisher/late/cli.py (existing cmd_batch patterns), src/publisher/tracking.py (is_already_published)_
  - _Requirements: 2, 4_
  - _Prompt: Role: CLI Developer with expertise in batch operations and progress reporting | Task: Add schedule auto command to CLI following requirements 2 and 4, using auto_schedule() from ScheduleManager and batch command patterns | Restrictions: Scan for video_*.mp4 files in outputs subdirectories, filter with is_already_published(), respect --start-slot parameter, use --dry-run for preview without publishing, display progress during scheduling, show final summary with counts | Success: Command scans videos correctly, filters published videos, auto-scheduling works with slot assignment, dry-run mode previews without side effects, summary is clear and accurate_

- [ ] 5.3. Add cleanup command to CLI
  - File: src/publisher/late/cli.py
  - Add cleanup subparser with --product-id, --all, --dry-run arguments
  - Implement cmd_cleanup() handler function
  - Create publisher client and CleanupManager
  - Handle --product-id for single cleanup or --all for batch
  - Display results with cleaned count, skipped count, disk space freed
  - Purpose: Provide manual cleanup command for on-demand operations
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/cleanup.py (CleanupManager.cleanup() and cleanup_all()), src/publisher/late/cli.py (existing command patterns), src/publisher/__init__.py (create_publisher)_
  - _Requirements: 6_
  - _Prompt: Role: CLI Developer with expertise in user confirmations and safety features | Task: Add cleanup command to CLI following requirement 6, using CleanupManager for operations and existing command patterns | Restrictions: Require either --product-id or --all (mutually exclusive), use --dry-run for preview, require explicit --confirm flag for --all mode, display disk space in human-readable format (MB/GB), show detailed results per product in verbose mode | Success: Command accepts correct argument combinations, --confirm requirement prevents accidental --all cleanup, dry-run works correctly, disk space is formatted readably, results are clear_

- [ ] 5.4. Add --no-cleanup flag to single and batch commands
  - File: src/publisher/late/cli.py
  - Add --no-cleanup argument to single_parser and batch_parser
  - Update cmd_single() to check cleanup config and --no-cleanup flag
  - Update cmd_batch() to check cleanup config and --no-cleanup flag
  - After successful publish: if cleanup.enabled and not args.no_cleanup, create CleanupManager and call cleanup()
  - Log cleanup results or log that cleanup was disabled via flag
  - Purpose: Integrate automatic cleanup with CLI override option
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/cleanup.py (CleanupManager.cleanup()), src/publisher/late/cli.py (cmd_single and cmd_batch from existing code), src/publisher/config.py (config.cleanup_config)_
  - _Requirements: 5, 7_
  - _Prompt: Role: CLI Developer with expertise in feature integration and conditional logic | Task: Add --no-cleanup flag and integrate automatic cleanup into single and batch commands following requirements 5 and 7, checking config.cleanup.enabled and args.no_cleanup flag | Restrictions: Only run cleanup after successful publish, respect both config flag and CLI flag (CLI overrides config), pass correct product_id and platforms to cleanup(), log cleanup disabled message if --no-cleanup used, handle cleanup failures without failing entire publish operation | Success: --no-cleanup flag works correctly, cleanup runs automatically when enabled, CLI flag overrides config, cleanup failures are logged but don't fail publish, user sees clear messages about cleanup status_

## Phase 6: Testing

- [ ] 6.1. Write unit tests for schedule models
  - File: tests/publisher/test_schedule_models.py
  - Test RecurringSlot.next_occurrence() with various day/time combinations
  - Test ScheduleEntry validation in __post_init__
  - Test ScheduleConfig validation rules
  - Test to_dict() serialization for all schedule models
  - Purpose: Ensure schedule data models work correctly
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/models.py (RecurringSlot, ScheduleEntry, ScheduleConfig), tests/publisher/test_models.py (existing test patterns)_
  - _Requirements: 2_
  - _Prompt: Role: QA Engineer with expertise in Python unit testing and pytest | Task: Write comprehensive unit tests for schedule models following requirement 2, testing validation, next_occurrence calculation, and serialization | Restrictions: Use pytest fixtures for test data, test both success and failure cases, verify __post_init__ validation raises ValueError, test timezone-aware datetime handling, ensure to_dict() produces valid JSON | Success: All model methods are tested with good coverage, edge cases like week boundaries are covered, validation tests confirm rules work, serialization tests verify JSON compatibility_

- [ ] 6.2. Write unit tests for ScheduleManager
  - File: tests/publisher/test_schedule_manager.py
  - Test _load_schedule() and _save_schedule() with mock filesystem
  - Test list_scheduled() with various filter combinations
  - Test get_next_slot() calculation accuracy
  - Test add_entry() atomic write behavior
  - Mock auto_schedule() external dependencies (publisher.publish)
  - Purpose: Ensure ScheduleManager operations work correctly
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/schedule.py (ScheduleManager), tests/publisher/test_tracking.py (file operation test patterns), pytest-mock for mocking_
  - _Requirements: 2, 4_
  - _Prompt: Role: QA Engineer with expertise in file I/O testing and mocking | Task: Write comprehensive unit tests for ScheduleManager following requirements 2 and 4, mocking filesystem and external dependencies | Restrictions: Use tmp_path fixture for temporary files, mock publisher.publish() to avoid API calls, test atomic write behavior (verify temp file + rename), test filter edge cases (empty results, all None filters), verify get_next_slot() handles timezone conversions | Success: All ScheduleManager methods tested with good coverage, file operations are tested with temp directories, external dependencies are properly mocked, edge cases like empty schedule files are covered_

- [ ] 6.3. Write unit tests for ScheduleValidator
  - File: tests/publisher/test_schedule_validator.py
  - Test validate() with valid and invalid entries
  - Test _is_duplicate() detection logic
  - Test _check_spacing() enforcement with same/different platforms
  - Test _check_daily_limit() counting logic
  - Test all validation rules (past schedules, timezone, etc.)
  - Purpose: Ensure schedule validation rules work correctly
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/schedule_validator.py (ScheduleValidator), src/publisher/models.py (ScheduleEntry)_
  - _Requirements: 3_
  - _Prompt: Role: QA Engineer with expertise in validation logic testing | Task: Write comprehensive unit tests for ScheduleValidator following requirement 3, testing all validation rules with success and failure scenarios | Restrictions: Create fixture entries with known timestamps for deterministic tests, test timezone-aware comparisons, verify error messages are descriptive, test boundary conditions (exactly N hours apart, exactly max daily limit), test each validation rule independently | Success: All validation rules tested thoroughly, error messages verified for clarity, boundary conditions covered, each validation method has dedicated tests_

- [ ] 6.4. Write unit tests for CleanupManager
  - File: tests/publisher/test_cleanup_manager.py
  - Test verify_publication() with mocked publisher.get_status()
  - Test archive_directory() with temporary directories
  - Test _log_cleanup() audit logging
  - Test cleanup() with all safety checks (enabled, verified, archived)
  - Test cleanup_all() batch operation
  - Purpose: Ensure cleanup operations work safely
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/cleanup.py (CleanupManager), pytest-asyncio for async tests, pytest-mock for mocking, tmp_path for temporary files_
  - _Requirements: 5, 6, 8_
  - _Prompt: Role: QA Engineer with expertise in async testing and file operations | Task: Write comprehensive unit tests for CleanupManager following requirements 5, 6, and 8, testing all safety checks and batch operations | Restrictions: Use pytest-asyncio for async method tests, mock publisher.get_status() to control verification results, use tmp_path for file operations, test dry_run mode without side effects, verify audit log entries are created, test archive creation without deleting real files | Success: All CleanupManager methods tested with async support, safety checks verified (enabled, verified, archived), dry_run mode confirmed to have no side effects, audit logging tested, batch operations covered_

- [ ] 6.5. Write integration tests for end-to-end workflows
  - File: tests/e2e/test_publisher_schedule_cleanup.py
  - Test full workflow: configure schedule → auto_schedule → publish → cleanup
  - Test calendar list with real schedule.json
  - Test cleanup verification with mock Late API
  - Test --no-cleanup flag override behavior
  - Purpose: Ensure all components work together correctly
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/late/cli.py (all commands), src/publisher/schedule.py, src/publisher/cleanup.py, pytest fixtures for test data_
  - _Requirements: All_
  - _Prompt: Role: QA Engineer with expertise in integration testing and end-to-end workflows | Task: Write integration tests covering complete workflows for all requirements, testing component interactions and CLI commands | Restrictions: Use pytest fixtures for test publisher client with mocked Late API, create real schedule.json and cleanup_audit.json in temp directories, test CLI argument parsing with argparse, verify file state after operations (schedule.json updated, directories removed), test error propagation through layers | Success: End-to-end workflows execute successfully, CLI commands work with real argument parsing, file state is correct after operations, error handling works across components, all features integrate smoothly_

- [ ] 6.6. Update existing batch publisher tests
  - File: tests/publisher/test_batch.py
  - Add tests for cleanup integration in BatchPublisher
  - Test that cleanup runs after successful batch publish when enabled
  - Test that --no-cleanup flag prevents cleanup in batch mode
  - Verify cleanup failures don't fail entire batch
  - Purpose: Ensure batch publisher works with cleanup feature
  - _Leverage: src/publisher/batch.py (BatchPublisher), tests/publisher/test_batch.py (existing tests), pytest-mock for cleanup mocking_
  - _Requirements: 5, 7_
  - _Prompt: Role: QA Engineer with expertise in regression testing and integration | Task: Update existing BatchPublisher tests to include cleanup integration following requirements 5 and 7, verifying cleanup runs correctly in batch mode | Restrictions: Extend existing tests without breaking them, mock CleanupManager to avoid file operations, verify cleanup is called with correct product_ids after successful publishes, test cleanup failures are logged but don't fail batch, verify --no-cleanup prevents cleanup calls | Success: Existing tests still pass, new cleanup tests verify integration, cleanup failures don't break batch processing, --no-cleanup flag is properly tested_
